summary: An excerpt from a space-opera novel (Book 15, part 159) in which Ray Marlowe, an EED officer, meets Rich Becker, who suspects classified intelligence leaks are being used to manipulate the New Holyoke run. Becker says Marlowe could be decorated or ruined if he proves Whiston financial backing of the Lilaiken movement. Ray then broods over Emma canceling their last shipboard date before hard deceleration, and over Frederick's control of her, while Kilgore appears in Marine shore-leave clothes.
one_line: Ray Marlowe, an EED officer, is warned about leaked intelligence and the Lilaiken movement while Emma cancels their final shipboard date before deceleration.
key_facts: Becker suspects the bad guys have access to too much classified intelligence on the New Holyoke run, which he says smells like manipulation.
Marlowe has given the Lilaikens plenty of reasons to want him out of the way, according to his dialogue with Becker.
Becker says that if Marlowe documents Whiston financial backing of the Lilaiken movement, he may receive a medal or have his career hung out to dry.
Ray had planned a last shipboard date with Emma that included dinner and the theatre.
The planned date also included a run up to the obs platform to view New Holyoke, as advertised in a flier circulated by the entertainment director.
Emma called Ray late in the morning to cancel the date, sounding distinctly unhappy, almost tearful.
Frederick told Emma the last night before hard deceleration on an interstellar run is inevitably raucous, with people becoming wild, drunken, and frenzied.
Frederick forbade Emma to leave and said she shouldn't be mixed up in the gathering.
Ray thinks Frederick knows plenty about orgies and that it is easier to protect little sister's virtue when you know what you're protecting it from.
Ray is attempting, with limited success, not to feel childish about the cancellation.
Emma has promised to tour Blackheath Grange with Ray on the ground.
Ray expects to be on New Holyoke for months, possibly years, if the EED does not get a handle on the Lilaikens.
Kilgore emerges from the short hallway leading back to the bedroom, half dressed, buttoning his shirt.
Kilgore has reverted to Marine-on-shore-leave attire, a loud shirt and tough khaki cargo pants.
